related_questions.question: How many days do I wait to take a COVID test?
related_questions.snippet: If you were exposed to someone who has COVID-19 and you do not have symptoms, wait at least 5 full days after your exposure before testing. If you test too early, you may have an inaccurate result. If you are in certain high-risk settings, you may need to test as part of a screening testing program.

related_questions.question: Can you test for COVID too late?
related_questions.snippet: Key takeaways: It's best to test for COVID-19 infection right away if you develop symptoms. Then test again after 48 hours if your first test was negative. If you don't have any symptoms but have been in close contact with someone with COVID infection, wait 5 days before testing.

related_questions.question: How long does it take for COVID symptoms to show up on a test?
related_questions.snippet: If you develop symptoms, get tested right away. Otherwise, wait five to seven days. COVID-19's incubation period lasts up to 14 days. If you have the virus, it takes time to build up in your system.
